note: The WAV/RIFF header supplies the attacker-controlled ADPCM block size into the IMA initialization path.
The requested block alignment is stored as the decoder's block size and later governs how many samples are decoded per block.
The header-provided samples-per-block value is retained and used to size the per-block decode loop.
The decoder iterates for the advertised number of samples, so a malformed header can drive more output writes than the actual block buffer supports.
Each loop body writes decoded PCM samples into the output buffer; with an inconsistent block layout this becomes a heap-buffer-overflow write in the block decode routine.
